title: Dry German Riesling
subtitle: The Pfalz's speciality
objectives: Explain the rise of dry German Riesling
Explain the role of trocken and GG

steps.title: A dry revolution
steps.body: For much of the 20th century, German Riesling abroad meant sweet. From the 1980s, Pfalz producers led a return to dry, trocken, Riesling, which had been traditional before. Today over two-thirds of German wine is dry or off-dry, and the Pfalz's warm climate makes balanced dry wines easier.

steps.title: The style
steps.body: Dry Pfalz Riesling is fuller and riper than Mosel or Rheingau Riesling, often 12.5 to 13.5% alcohol, with stone fruit, citrus, spice and minerality from sandstone, limestone or basalt. GG wines from top sites, like Forster Kirchenstück, Forster Jesuitengarten and Deidesheimer Hohenmorgen, can age 10 to 20 years.

steps.prompt: How does dry Pfalz Riesling typically compare with Mosel Riesling?
steps.explanation: A warmer climate gives more body and ripeness.

steps.title: Basalt and sites
steps.body: Forst's top vineyards have basalt, volcanic rock, which absorbs heat and gives intense, spicy, mineral wines. Kirchenstück, a small walled site in Forst, is often considered one of Germany's finest dry Riesling vineyards. Labels name village and vineyard, like Forster Pechstein.

steps.explanation: Wehlener Sonnenuhr is in the Mosel.

steps.title: What you learned
points: The Pfalz led the return to dry German Riesling
Its dry Riesling is riper and fuller
Basalt sites in Forst give some of Germany's best
